newsitem.title: USA: Lucent sees neutral venture earnings impact.
newsitem.headline: Lucent sees neutral venture earnings impact.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc's newly announced joint venture with Philips Electronics NV will have a neutral impact on Lucent's overall earnings in 1997, an executive with the U.S. telecom equipment maker said.
Carly Fiorina, the head of Lucent's existing consumer products business, said the impact of the Philips venture will be neutral on Lucent's overall earnings results in 1997.

In addition, the venture is expected to add to Philips earnings in the year going forward, said Michael McTighe, managing director of Philips consumer products business and chief executive of the newly formed joint venture.
"From a Philips perspective, we expect the joint venture to have a positive impact on the year going forward," McTighe said. The joint venture takes effect October 1, 1997.
The two executives were responding to reporters' questions during a conference call Tuesday afternoon.
"This joint venture will be profitable from day one," McTighe added. The venture will have combined revenues of $2.5 billion, the officials said.
The Lucent officials's comments referred to the company's fiscal year ending in September 1997, a spokeswoman said.

During the call, Fiorina said all Lucent consumer products would be merged into the venture and sold under the Philips brand, after what she called an "orderly transition" period to ensure that retailers and consumers understand the changes.

The Lucent executive said the venture reinforced efforts by Lucent to focus on its network infrastructure business instead of consumer products, while allowing Philips to emphasize its consumer products operations.

She said Lucent last year had purchased two Philips cellular infrastructure businesses using the international GSM standard, allowing Lucent to become more active in building wireless network systems in Europe.
The venture merges the existing consumer businesses and involves no cash transactions between the two, officials said. Philips owns 60 percent and Lucent owns 40 percent.

Both parent companies plan to supply additional funding to develop the joint venture. They will also continue to provide the venture access to other operations, such as Lucent's research and development and network systems businesses.
"The partnerships we are forming with Philips is a near-perfect fit for both companies," Fiorina said. "What each company needed was exactly what the other company had."
Fiorina will serve as a board member of the new venture, but will have no operating responsibilities.
McTighe's statement regarding earnings in the year going forward referred to Philips' calendar year beginning in January 1998.
Lucent stock was up 2-7/8 at 70-3/4 by midafternoon. Philips shares closed in Amsterdam up 7.90 guilders at 128.90.
